answer_value: Either conclusion II or III follows
steps: Lotus is inside Tulip, which is inside Sunflower; Lotus and Daisy are disjoint
I (All D are T) not forced
II (Some S are D) and III (No S is D) are each possible but neither is forced, and they form a complementary pair
So either II or III follows
check_code:
from itertools import product
# regions: subsets of {L,D,T,S} membership; universe atoms = 16 types, model = which types are nonempty
types=list(product([0,1],repeat=4))  # (L,D,T,S)
def ok(m):
    if not m: return False
    for (L,D,T,S) in m:
        if L and D: return False
        if L and not T: return False
        if T and not S: return False
    return any(t[0] for t in m) and any(t[1] for t in m)
I_all=II_all=III_all=True; either=True; I_poss=II_poss=III_poss=False
import itertools
for mask in range(1,1<<16):
    m=[types[i] for i in range(16) if mask>>i&1]
    if not ok(m): continue
    I=all(t[2] for t in m if t[1]); II=any(t[3] and t[1] for t in m); III=not II
    I_all&=I; II_all&=II; III_all&=III; either&=(II or III)
res={"A":II_all and not I_all and not III_all,"B":(not II_all) and (not III_all) and either,"C":I_all and not II_all and not III_all,"D":III_all and not I_all and not II_all}
assert res["B"]
for k in "ACD": assert not res[k]

from fractions import Fraction as F
def val(a,b):
    sw=lambda x: b if x==a else a if x==b else x
    e1=sw(57)-F(sw(33),sw(11))*sw(13)-sw(2)
    e2=sw(64)-F(sw(56),sw(8))*sw(4)-sw(44)
    return F(sw(2))**e1+F(3)**e2 if e1.denominator==1 and e2.denominator==1 else None
res={"A":val(2,4),"B":val(56,57),"C":val(57,64),"D":val(33,44)}
assert res["D"]==35
for k in "ABC": assert res[k]!=35
